name: Madame Zoria
origin: Lands beyond Cador and the Eccentric East
appearance: An elderly tiefling woman with a deeply lined face, curling horns adorned with small charms, and a rather eclectic assortment of shawls, scarves, and jewelry accumulated over a lifetime of wandering. Madame Zoria maintains a cramped, dimly lit alcove within the Wayward Spur, filled with books, maps, strange trinkets, half-melted candles, and magical implements of questionable authenticity. She consults her crystal ball, reads her tarokka cards, and plays her accordion in roughly equal measure.
portrayal: Madame Zoria is eccentric, theatrical, and mischievously enigmatic. She has a tendency to speak in metaphors, digress into seemingly unrelated anecdotes, and interrupt conversations to acknowledge some omen that has escaped everyone else's notice. She treats even the most mundane coincidences with great significance, though whether she genuinely believes all her superstitions is difficult to ascertain. Beneath her peculiarities lies a remarkably perceptive woman with a great deal of worldly experience and a genuine affection for the younger adventurers of the League.
motivations: Zoria is fascinated by the workings of fate and the seemingly insignificant decisions that shape the lives of mortals. She delights in observing the fortunes of the League's adventurers and takes particular interest in those who appear to be destined for extraordinary things. She is also an avid collector of peculiar artifacts, obscure folklore, and unusual methods of divination, irrespective of their demonstrable efficacy.
personal_circumstances: Madame Zoria spent much of her long life adventuring, traveling to distant and often inhospitable lands. Among her more extraordinary exploits was a sojourn in a mist-shrouded realm ruled by a vampiric overlord from his looming castle. Her experiences have afforded her considerable familiarity with supernatural creatures, ancient curses, forgotten traditions, and the peculiar ways in which magic manifests throughout the world. Though retired from adventuring, she continues to indulge her curiosity through the accounts and discoveries of League members.
relationships: Zoria is particularly fond of Flopthar, whose willingness to entertain her superstitions provides her with endless amusement. She respects Sazerac's discipline but enjoys challenging his conviction that one's destiny is determined solely by one's actions. Tabitha's skepticism toward divination is a source of considerable entertainment, and Zoria occasionally offers unsolicited predictions concerning the spectacular failure of her latest inventions. She shares a warm familiarity with Floyd, though she seldom offers a straightforward account of how the two became acquainted.
knowledge_and_rumors: Madame Zoria offers interpretations of unusual artifacts, knowledge of local legends and supernatural phenomena, and fortunes read from dice, tarokka cards, bones, or her crystal ball. Her predictions are frequently frustrating in their ambiguity, though occasionally unsettling in their accuracy. While considerably knowledgeable, Zoria is by no means omniscient. When confronted with unfamiliar mysteries, she is more likely to direct adventurers toward obscure texts, knowledgeable individuals, or locations of historical significance than to provide definitive answers herself.

Madame Zoria — Fortuneteller
Chaotic Good, female tiefling, elderly

Appearance. An elderly tiefling woman with a deeply lined face, curling horns adorned with
small charms, and a rather eclectic assortment of shawls, scarves, and jewelry accumulated
over a lifetime of wandering. Madame Zoria maintains a cramped, dimly lit alcove within the
Wayward Spur, filled with books, maps, strange trinkets, half-melted candles, and magical
implements of questionable authenticity. She consults her crystal ball, reads her tarokka cards,
and plays her accordion in roughly equal measure.

Portrayal. Madame Zoria is eccentric, theatrical, and mischievously enigmatic. She has a
tendency to speak in metaphors, digress into seemingly unrelated anecdotes, and interrupt
conversations to acknowledge some omen that has escaped everyone else's notice. She treats
even the most mundane coincidences with great significance, though whether she genuinely
believes all her superstitions is difficult to ascertain. Beneath her peculiarities lies a remarkably
perceptive woman with a great deal of worldly experience and a genuine affection for the
younger adventurers of the League.

Background. Madame Zoria spent much of her long life adventuring, traveling to distant and
often inhospitable lands. Among her more extraordinary exploits was a sojourn in a
mist-shrouded realm ruled by a vampiric overlord from his looming castle. Her experiences have
afforded her considerable familiarity with supernatural creatures, ancient curses, forgotten
traditions, and the peculiar ways in which magic manifests throughout the world. Though retired
from adventuring, she continues to indulge her curiosity through the accounts and discoveries of
League members.

Motivations. Zoria is fascinated by the workings of fate and the seemingly insignificant
decisions that shape the lives of mortals. She delights in observing the fortunes of the League's
adventurers and takes particular interest in those who appear to be destined for extraordinary
things. She is also an avid collector of peculiar artifacts, obscure folklore, and unusual methods
of divination, irrespective of their demonstrable efficacy.

Relationships. Zoria is particularly fond of Flopthar, whose willingness to entertain her
superstitions provides her with endless amusement. She respects Sazerac's discipline but
enjoys challenging his conviction that one's destiny is determined solely by one's actions.
Tabitha's skepticism toward divination is a source of considerable entertainment, and Zoria
occasionally offers unsolicited predictions concerning the spectacular failure of her latest
inventions. She shares a warm familiarity with Floyd, though she seldom offers a straightforward
account of how the two became acquainted.

Services and Expertise. Madame Zoria offers interpretations of unusual artifacts, knowledge of
local legends and supernatural phenomena, and fortunes read from dice, tarokka cards, bones,
or her crystal ball. Her predictions are frequently frustrating in their ambiguity, though
occasionally unsettling in their accuracy. While considerably knowledgeable, Zoria is by no
means omniscient. When confronted with unfamiliar mysteries, she is more likely to direct

adventurers toward obscure texts, knowledgeable individuals, or locations of historical
significance than to provide definitive answers herself.

Adventure Hooks.

   ●​ The Missing Card. During an otherwise ordinary reading, Zoria discovers a tarokka card
      among her deck that she does not recognize. Its illustration bears a striking resemblance
      to a location somewhere in the Eccentric East. She asks the adventurers to investigate
      the place, though she is unusually reluctant to speculate upon the card's meaning.
   ●​ A Familiar Mist. Accounts of an isolated frontier settlement periodically enveloped in an
      unnatural mist remind Zoria of her adventures in a distant land. Troubled by the
      similarities, she asks the adventurers to investigate the phenomenon and return with an
      account of what they discover. She hopes, rather emphatically, that her suspicions are
      unfounded.
